examples.title: Linear inequalities
steps: Multiply all three parts by 3: 6 < 5 − x ≤ 12.
Multiply by −1 and flip both signs: −7 ≤ x < −1.

examples.title: Quadratic inequalities
steps: The x² term is positive, so the expression is positive outside the roots and zero at them.

examples.title: Modulus inequalities
steps: 2x + 1 is more than 7 away from 0, so 2x + 1 > 7 or 2x + 1 < −7.
The first gives x > 3. The second gives 2x < −8, so x < −4.

examples.title: Sum of moduli
steps: Pair the outer points: |x + 2| + |x − 10| is at least 12, the distance from −2 to 10.
Pair the inner points: |x − 3| + |x − 7| is at least 4, the distance from 3 to 7.
Both least values hold together for any x from 3 to 7, so the least total is 12 + 4 = 16.

examples.title: AM-GM
examples.problem: a, b and c are positive numbers with a + b + c = 15. What is the largest possible value of abc?
steps: The value 125 is reached when a = b = c = 5.
